wallet.heading: Get a wallet
wallet.description: Choose a wallet that fits how you plan to hold and use KAS.

safety.label: Important:
safety.body: Back up your recovery phrase or wallet instructions before moving meaningful funds. Send a small test transaction first, then move the rest only after it arrives.

buy.heading: Buy KAS
buy.description: KAS is listed on many exchanges. Acquire it on a platform supported in your region, then transfer it to your private wallet.

transfer.heading: Take custody of your KAS
transfer.description: Secure your assets by transferring them from the exchange to your private wallet.
transfer.screenReaderDiagram: KAS moving from an exchange account to a private wallet

receiveAddress.title: Get your receive address
receiveAddress.description: Open your wallet, choose 'Receive', and copy your address.

testTransaction.title: Send a test transaction
testTransaction.description: Withdraw a tiny fraction of KAS from the exchange to verify the route is correct.

balance.title: Transfer the balance
balance.description: Once the test transaction arrives safely in your wallet, withdraw the remaining balance.

waitTimes.label: Exchange wait times:
waitTimes.body: Kaspa transfers are fast, but exchanges may apply delays or withdrawal holds. Check your withdrawal status and the exchange’s guidance.

security.label: Security Check:
security.body: Always verify the first and last few characters of your address before confirming.

help.heading: Keep moving
help.descriptionWithAi: Ask Kaspa AI for instant answers on wallets, buying, and safety. For community help join Discord, or check a transaction on the explorer.
help.descriptionWithoutAi: For community help join Discord, or check a transaction on the explorer.

control.label: Control
control.short: No third party can freeze or take your funds.
control.description: Some wallets give you full control over your KAS. This means no third party can freeze or take away your funds. You are still responsible, however, for securing and backing up your wallet.

validation.label: Validation
validation.short: Run or choose the Kaspa node your wallet uses.
validation.description: Some wallets let you control which Kaspa node processes your transactions, either by running their own, or by letting you point them at any node you trust.

transparency.label: Transparency
transparency.short: Public source code that anyone can inspect.
transparency.description: Some wallets are open-source and can be built deterministically, a process of compiling software which ensures the resulting code can be reproduced to help ensure it hasn't been tampered with.

fees.label: Fees
fees.short: Choose the network fee you pay.
fees.description: Some wallets give you full control over setting the fee paid to the Kaspa network before making a transaction, to ensure that your transactions are confirmed in a timely manner without paying more than you have to.

two_fa.label: 2FA
two_fa.short: Require a second code to access your funds.
two_fa.description: Two-factor authentication (2FA) adds a second layer of security to your wallet. Beyond your password, a verification code from an app or text message is required to access your funds. Note that 2FA typically relies on a third-party service to provide the verification.

hardware_wallet.label: Hardware wallet support
hardware_wallet.short: Pair with a device that keeps your keys offline.
hardware_wallet.description: Some software wallets can pair with a hardware wallet device (e.g. Ledger or Tangem), letting you keep your private keys isolated on the device while still using a familiar software interface.

multisig.label: Multisig
multisig.short: Require more than one key to move funds.
multisig.description: Some wallets support multi-signature transactions, which require more than one key to authorize a transfer. This can be used to divide responsibility across multiple parties or add an extra layer of protection for high-value holdings.

hashed_addresses.label: Hashed addresses (P2SH)
hashed_addresses.short: Keep your public key hidden until you spend.
hashed_addresses.description: Standard Kaspa addresses reveal your public key. Pay-to-script-hash (P2SH) addresses keep it hidden behind a hash until you spend, adding protection against future attacks on public-key cryptography, such as from quantum computers. Spending reveals the key, so move any remaining funds to a fresh hashed address.

ratings.mixedExplanation: This rating varies across the selected platforms.

control.good: Self-custodial. You hold your private keys, so no third party can freeze or seize your funds.
control.caution: A third party holds the private keys, or user control over them has not been verified.

validation.good: Runs its own full Kaspa node by default, so it validates transactions independently.
validation.acceptable: Lets you point it at any Kaspa node you trust, but cannot run as a node itself.
validation.caution: Uses wallet-selected Kaspa nodes, or user-selectable nodes have not been verified.
validation.not_applicable: The hardware device signs transactions, while companion software handles network access and validation.

transparency.good: The code is public, and independent checks can verify that the released software was built from it.
transparency.acceptable: The required source is public, but independent reproduction of the released build has not been verified.
transparency.mixed: Required parts of this wallet have different transparency levels.
transparency.caution: Full source for the required app or firmware is unavailable, incomplete, or has not been verified.

fees.good: Lets you set an arbitrary custom fee on each transaction.
fees.acceptable: Offers preset fee tiers, but does not let you set a fully custom fee.
fees.caution: Kaspa fee choices are unavailable, unclear, or have not been verified.
